key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize building energy management and battery charging more effectively when it is paired with post-hoc explanations that reveal why the controller acts as it does.
engineering_relevance: For PV-equipped buildings, this approach offers a practical way to cut electricity costs while improving operator trust in autonomous energy control systems.
method: Train on-policy and off-policy DRL agents on an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, tariffs, weather, calendars, and forecasts.
Compare A2C and PPO against off-policy methods for reward and policy stability.
Use post-hoc interpretation techniques to explain learned control policies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, with A2C and PPO performing best in cumulative rewards and stability.
watch_item: Explainability is post-hoc, so the insights depend on the fidelity of the explanation method and may not fully capture the true internal policy logic.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
